records.name: Collaborative Cataloging Japan
records.summary: A nonprofit that preserves and shares Japanese experimental film and video. It runs an online viewing library, publishes essays and books, holds exhibitions, and hosts artist talks.
records.what_you_do: Watch works in the online viewing library, join the members' viewings and artist talks, or become a member for the monthly feature. The site does not mention classes, workshops or volunteer jobs.

schedule.text: A new monthly feature on the online viewing platform for members, plus members' viewings and talks at set times (for example a members' viewing running September 10 to November 1, 2026)

locations.label: Office (address from the batch list, see notes)

cost.text: Membership and event prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Browse the viewing library and blog, then join as a member through the sign-up link to get the monthly feature and members' viewings
first_step.basis: Open to anyone online with a clear sign-up link; membership is the only stated way to get the member features.

records.notes: The group's website shows a placeholder street address, phone and email, so the address above comes from the batch list (IRS and Cultural Fund records), not the site. Confirm before publishing. Its work is international and based in Philadelphia; the public can take part online from anywhere. Newest dated items: a members' viewing September 10 to November 1, 2026, and a blog post July 19, 2026.

records.name: Ebenezer Maxwell Mansion
records.summary: A Victorian house museum in Germantown that shows nineteenth century home life through its rooms, gardens and collections. It also runs guided tours, live Victorian theatre, lectures and family events.
records.what_you_do: Take a guided house tour, come to the free or paid concerts, theatre shows and family events, or volunteer through the museum's volunteer page.

schedule.text: Tours on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays at noon, 1, 2 and 3 pm; Thursday tours by advance reservation only; events through the fall, and a Victorian Christmas tour season from December 4, 2026 to January 10, 2027

cost.text: Tours are $10 per person. Several events are free, such as the October 31 trick or treat; other events are priced separately.

first_step.how: Come on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday for a tour at noon, 1, 2 or 3 pm ($10 per person), or email the museum to ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: Public tours and events with no application, and the site gives a clear way to volunteer and to join.

records.notes: The site lists events without years; the weekdays match 2026. The newsletter archive on the site runs only to 2022, but the event listings are current. Partner events from the Historic Germantown calendar were not checked here.

records.name: Enchantment Theatre Company
records.notes: Touring theatre company for young audiences. Its public role is buying a ticket to a show. Schools and venues book its performances and the Enchantment Everywhere program, and donors can give, but the site lists no classes, workshops, auditions, volunteer roles, membership or community program open to the public. Per the brief, a company whose only public role is buying a ticket is not_a_group. The 2026 to 2027 national tour of Harold and the Purple Crayon is announced without dates, and the site's Fringe Festival and repertory season dates are inconsistent, so no last sign of life is recorded. Revisit if a class, workshop or volunteer role appears.

records.name: Germantown Community Broadcasting
records.summary: The community radio station for Germantown, on the air as G-Town Radio at 92.9 (WGGT-LP). It runs local live shows and podcasts, and it hosts artist residencies with public gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Tune in to live shows and podcasts, come to the public gatherings for the current artist residency, or ask the station how to get involved in its programs.

schedule.text: Live shows run in the morning and at midday (for example 8 to 10 am, 10 to 11 am, 11 am to 12 pm, and noon to 1 pm); three artist residency gatherings were announced for August 2026, with more dates to come on the site

cost.text: The site lists no prices for listening, events or membership.

first_step.how: Listen online at gtownradio.com, then email info@gtownradio.com or call 215.609.4301 to ask how to volunteer as a host or producer
first_step.basis: The Get Involved section says 'Volunteer Today' but gives no details on roles or how to start, so the way in is unclear beyond contacting the station.

records.notes: The Get Involved page has a 'Volunteer Today' headline but no details on hosting, producing, training or membership, so the volunteer route is not confirmed beyond contacting the station. The schedule gives times only with no days. The batch name is Germantown Community Broadcasting and the on-air name is G-Town Radio. The vocabulary has no radio tag, so the category is a best fit. The site says no upcoming programs are listed right now.

records.name: Historic Fair Hill
records.summary: A community organization in the Fairhill neighborhood that cares for a historic Quaker burial ground and works with local schools on early reading and urban greening. It also runs family events, a cooking class and a farmers market.
records.what_you_do: Read with children as a reading buddy, help in a school library or garden, plant trees, help run events, or come to the family events, the cooking class and the farmers market.

schedule.text: Family Fun Saturdays, afternoons on Saturdays from April 4 to November 21, 2026; an Open Fire Cooking Class and Pancake Party on October 17, 12:30 to 2 pm; the 19133 Farmer's Market on October 30, 10 am to noon

locations.label: Village of Arts and Humanities (farmers market)

cost.text: The cooking class is free. The farmers market is pay what you wish, and Historic Fair Hill's produce is always free. The cost of Family Fun Saturdays is not listed.

first_step.how: Come to the free Open Fire Cooking Class and Pancake Party on October 17, 12:30 to 2 pm, open to all ages; or email info@historicfairhill.com to ask about becoming a reading buddy
first_step.basis: Free events open to all ages, and the site lists several volunteer roles with a contact address.

records.notes: The batch lists the kind as congregation, but the site describes a community and historic-site organization, so kind is set to nonprofit. Hours are not stated on the site. The August 12, 2026 news items show titles only (Fair Hill Solar, Growing Lifelong Readers, a staff profile), so the summary relies on the events list. Newsletter signup and donations are through a PayPal link.

records.name: Historic Germantown Preserved
records.summary: A partnership of about 20 historic houses, sites and museums in Northwest Philadelphia that protects and shares Germantown's history. It runs walking tours, free and ticketed events, and a volunteer kitchen garden at Wyck.
records.what_you_do: Join a walking or house tour, come to the free events, or volunteer at Wyck's Home Farm Club, a kitchen garden where helpers take home a share of the produce.

schedule.text: Many events each month through the fall, including Home Farm Club volunteer mornings at Wyck (for example October 9, 10 am to noon, no registration), 26 walking tours planned for 2026, and a Visitor Center open 12 to 4 pm on listed dates

cost.text: Many events are free, such as Home Farm Club and the Wyck flax processing demonstrations. Some tours and events are paid: the October 10 Cliveden walking tour is $20, or $10 for members and residents of 19119 and 19144.

first_step.how: Come to the free Home Farm Club volunteer morning at Wyck on October 9, 10 am to noon, no registration needed
first_step.basis: Free public events and a volunteer garden day with no registration; the site does not say how beginners are welcomed.

records.notes: The site gives two different end dates for the rotating Visitor Center exhibit (December 1, 2026 and December 1, 2027), so those dates are not used. Partner sites named on the events list (Cliveden, Stenton, Awbury Arboretum, Johnson House, Germantown Historical Society, Hood Cemetery, La Salle University Art Museum) were seen but not added to leads_only or fetched, since they are outside this batch. Wyck Association is a separate record in this batch. The mailing address (6711 Germantown Ave, Suite 4936, 19119) is not a place to visit.

records.name: International Ballet Exchange
records.summary: A nonprofit ballet organization listed among Philadelphia Cultural Fund grantees. Its own website could not be read in this run, so what it offers the public is not confirmed.

locations.label: Address on the batch list (IRS and Cultural Fund records, not confirmed on a website)

records.notes: The website https://www.internationalballet.com redirected to a parked domain page offering the name for sale (GoDaddy). The redirect was not followed. The group's own site may have lapsed, so its current activity and public role are unknown. The source is the Cultural Fund grantee list (lead id above); the batch does not record a public URL for that list. Recheck the group directly before publishing.

records.name: Lest We Forget Slavery Museum
records.summary: A museum in Germantown about the history of slavery, with objects such as shackles and bills of sale and panels that explain the period. It also takes a traveling exhibit to schools and community events.
records.what_you_do: Book a tour at least 24 hours ahead, ask for the traveling exhibit for a school, congregation or community event, or join or give to support the museum's preservation work. The site describes no volunteer program.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday 10 am to 4 pm and Sunday noon to 4 pm; tours by appointment booked at least 24 hours ahead. No upcoming events are listed.

cost.text: No admission fee is mentioned on the page. Memberships and donations support the museum.

first_step.how: Book a tour by phone or email at least 24 hours ahead at (215) 205-4324 or info@lwfsm.com, or ask about the traveling exhibit for your school or group
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a clear way to book; tours are by appointment only, so there are no walk-ins.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a September 27, 2016 audio interview, older than 24 months, so status is dormant. The hours and contacts on the site look current and the 'Upcoming Events' section is empty. A reviewer should decide whether to show a dormant group. Batch alias: Lest We Forget Black Holocaust Museum. The site's second phone number is (215) 397-6060. The site describes no volunteer program.

records.name: Lyric Fest
records.notes: Presents concerts of vocal music, with a 2026 to 2027 season (November 2026, February 2027 and April 2027 concerts listed). The public role found on the site is buying concert tickets, donating and joining the mailing list. No class, workshop, audition, volunteer role, membership or community program was found, so per the brief it is not_a_group. Revisit if a community program is added. Address on the site and batch: 312 Carpenter Lane, Philadelphia, 19119.

records.name: Mamadêlê Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts foundation that teaches and performs the music, dance and culture of Bahia, Brazil. Its ensembles perform, it runs adult community classes and youth education programs, and it leads trips to Bahia.
records.what_you_do: Take an adult community class (including percussion), come to a performance or a free workshop series, sign up for the newsletter, or join a trip to Bahia. Donors can support the youth education programs.

schedule.text: An October 2026 four-part free workshop series on Afro-Brazilian percussion traditions (first session dated October 3, 2026) at Dendezeiros Studio; adult community classes and residencies run on dates the site does not list

cost.text: The October 2026 workshop series is free. Class and trip prices are not listed; donations are suggested at $25 to $500, or a custom amount.

first_step.how: Sign up for the foundation's newsletter, then ask about the adult community classes at Dendezeiros Studio, 224 West Walnut Lane
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a clear newsletter sign-up and a free workshop series; beginner status for the classes is not stated.

records.notes: The batch website http://www.mamadele.org permanently redirects to https://www.mamadele.com/new/, which is used here. The site confirms the studio address in the batch. Donation amounts are suggestions, not fees. Adult classes are a public way in, but their schedule and prices are not on the page, so ask the foundation. Volunteering and membership are not mentioned.

records.name: Mt. Airy Art Garage
records.summary: A nonprofit art space in Mt. Airy with a gallery, weekly and monthly art groups, jazz jams and concerts, and community festivals. Visitors can see the gallery shows and join its clubs and music nights.
records.what_you_do: Join the weekly Figure Drawing Group, the Collage Club or the Photo Club, come to the Third Wednesday jazz jam or a concert (musicians can sit in), or see the gallery shows. The site also has pages for membership and volunteering.

schedule.text: Figure Drawing Group weekly on Thursdays, 6:30 to 9:30 pm; Collage Club on the second and fourth Fridays, 6 to 8 pm (October dates are the 9th and 23rd); Third Wednesday jazz jam, doors 5:30 pm and music 6 pm; Photo Club monthly meetings; gallery open Wednesday to Saturday noon to 6 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm

locations.label: Mt. Airy Art Garage (Solomon Levy Gallery)

cost.text: Figure Drawing Group $15 a session; Collage Club $10; Photo Club $5 a meeting; jazz jam $15 general, $10 for members, and $5 to play. Gallery admission is not stated; a recent concert was $15 in advance and $20 at the door.

first_step.how: Come to the Collage Club on Friday, October 9 or October 23, 6 to 8 pm, $10; no experience is needed and supplies are provided
first_step.basis: The Collage Club says no experience is needed and supplies are provided, and the site lists a clear way to join the other groups.

records.notes: The site has pages for membership, donating and volunteering, but fees and details were not on the page read, so they are not recorded. The earlier liveness check recorded newest date 2026-09; this read shows an October 4, 2026 concert in its recent list, so last sign of life is set to 2026-10. Monday and Tuesday gallery hours are not listed. Exhibit admission is not stated. The Figure Drawing Group entrance is from the Mt. Pleasant Avenue driveway, and the site asks people to email first.

records.name: Network for New Music
records.summary: A Philadelphia new music ensemble that performs contemporary concerts and runs an education program. The program brings workshops to school classrooms, offers residencies to university composers, and runs a paid double bass ensemble.
records.what_you_do: Attend the season's concerts, watch for the open call for double bass players to join the paid ensemble, or donate. School workshops and university residencies are arranged through schools and universities, not by individuals.

schedule.text: Concerts follow a season; the site lists 2025 to 2026 as ended and 2026 to 2027 (Outside the Lines) as upcoming, with no dates on the pages read. The double bass ensemble call for players is open, with no date shown.

locations.label: Batch address (the site shows placeholder text)

cost.text: No concert ticket prices are listed. School workshops are listed at $200 to $500 each, and free for School District of Philadelphia classrooms.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a concert in the season, or email education@networkfornewmusic.org to ask about the next call for double bass players
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public; joining the paid ensemble needs a call and audition, so that route is for players only.

records.notes: Judgment call: the only public routes found are concerts, donations and the paid double bass ensemble, plus school and university programs that individuals cannot sign up for. The brief's ticket-only rule does not quite fit because of the open call for players and the community ensemble language, so the record is publish. A reviewer could reclassify it to not_a_group. The site shows placeholder address and phone text, so the batch address is used. The education page also lists a summer composition period for school musicians with All City Orchestra. The status is probably active because the pages carry a season label but no dated items.

records.name: Philadelphia Dance Theatre
records.summary: A classical ballet school and performing company in Mount Airy, founded in 1998. Its training runs from preschool through adult classes, and its company dances an annual Nutcracker and a spring new-works show.
records.what_you_do: Enroll in ballet classes for ages 3 and up, take the free trial class first, join the tuition-free boys' program, or come to the company's Nutcracker and spring shows.

schedule.text: Ballet classes run through the school year (fall classes started September 12, 2026); Nutcracker auditions were held in late September and early October; the company performs A Philadelphia Nutcracker each December and a spring new-works show

cost.text: The first class is free, siblings get 15 percent off family tuition, and the boys' program is tuition-free. Tuition prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Fill in the class recommendation form on the site, take the free trial class, then register through the studio's Dance StudioPro portal
first_step.basis: The site has a free first class and a set path for newcomers (form, trial class, placement), and classes are open to the public.

records.notes: The site gives days and months with no year; 2026 is inferred from its '26/27 Performance Season' label. Volunteering appears only as a testimonial with no sign-up; membership and open rehearsals are not mentioned. The batch address has a box number suffix, which is dropped; the site gives 7500 Germantown Ave, used here. The company also performs as a member of Regional Dance America Northeast.

records.name: Philadelphia Furniture Workshop
records.summary: A woodworking school in Philadelphia that teaches furniture making through project classes, short tool courses and beginner courses. Classes are small and taught by experienced furniture makers.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner course, a learning series, a project class or a short course on a tool or technique. The site also lists a newsletter sign-up.

schedule.text: Multi-week evening classes (for example Monday 6 to 9 pm for eight weeks) and weekend courses (9 am to 4 pm); the next listed sessions start September 12 and 17, 2026, and more classes will be scheduled

cost.text: Listed classes cost $425 to $1,425 each, depending on length. The site does not list shop hours or a drop-in fee.

first_step.how: Pick a beginner course or learning series from the class list (the Andon lamp weekend on December 5 and 6, 2026 is $550), or sign up for the newsletter to hear when new classes open
first_step.basis: The site offers beginner courses and a learning series, and says classes are small and taught by experienced makers.

records.notes: The class calendar lists 2026 sessions from September to December, and the site mentions a June 2026 Fine Woodworking feature. The batch says nonprofit; the site does not say so, so the kind comes from the batch list. Some listed classes are sold out. Open studio, volunteering and membership are not mentioned; the 'Support Us' page is linked but its contents were not shown.

records.name: Wildflower Composers
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs a summer composition festival for young composers aged 13 to 19 who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer. Students take seminars and lessons at Temple University, workshop new pieces with musicians, and hear their work premiered.
records.what_you_do: Apply to the two-week summer festival, where students take seminars and lessons, write a new piece, and work with musicians from Network for New Music. Donors can also support the work. The site lists no volunteer roles.

schedule.text: A two-week summer festival each July on the Temple University campus (the 2026 session was listed for July 6 to 17); online mini-courses and a lab are listed without dates

cost.text: No application fee. Tuition is $900, and dorm room and board add $1,400. Financial aid, including full scholarships, is available.

first_step.how: Apply through the festival's 'Learn more and apply' page, or ask about financial aid before you apply
first_step.basis: The festival needs an application and an eligibility check (students aged 13 to 19 who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer), but the site says no composition experience is required and financial aid is available.

records.notes: The festival page gives July 6 to 17, 2026 and says admissions stay open until filled with three spots left. That does not square with a July session that has already run, so check before sharing. Eligibility per the festival page: students aged 13 to 19 who are women, transgender, nonbinary or genderqueer, and able to read music in at least one clef. The homepage describes early-career composers, but the festival page's age range is used. The only email on the site appears to be a person's address, so it is not recorded; use the site's Contact page. Batch alias: Young Women Composers. The office address (22 E Clapier St, 19144) comes from the batch list and is not confirmed on the site.

records.name: Wyck Association
records.summary: The group that cares for Wyck, a National Historic Landmark house, garden and farm in Germantown that the Wistar and Haines families lived in for nine generations. It runs history, garden and urban farming programs.
records.what_you_do: Walk the free grounds, take a house tour, come to a Second Saturday workshop, or join the Home Farm Club, a volunteer kitchen garden where helpers share the produce. The site also lists membership and rentals.

schedule.text: Grounds open Tuesday to Friday 10 am to 4 pm and Saturday noon to 4 pm; house tours Thursday to Saturday noon to 4 pm; Home Farm Club volunteer mornings (October 9, 10 am to noon, per Historic Germantown Preserved's calendar); Second Saturday workshop series, dates not listed

cost.text: Grounds visits are free. House tour, workshop, membership and rental prices are not stated on the page.

first_step.how: Visit the free grounds during opening hours, or come to the Home Farm Club volunteer morning on October 9, 10 am to noon
first_step.basis: Free grounds and listed volunteer mornings are open to the public, but the Get Involved and membership pages could not be read.

records.notes: Wyck's own site has no dated items. The 2026 status comes from Historic Germantown Preserved's events list, which names Wyck events in October and November 2026 (Home Farm Club, a Crocktoberfest workshop, and flax processing demonstrations). The address 6026 Germantown Ave comes from the batch list; the site's address page was not read. The Get Involved page was linked, but a guessed URL returned 404, so volunteer and membership details are not recorded. Historic Germantown Preserved is a separate record.

records.name: Yes! And... Collaborative Arts
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that uses performing arts to build confidence, voice and community in children and teens from kindergarten through 12th grade. It runs year-round classes, summer camps and Shadow Company, a youth arts group for high schoolers.
records.what_you_do: Enroll a child in a year-round class or a summer theatre or imagination camp, have a high school student join Shadow Company, come to a youth show, or support the work through volunteering, sponsorship or giving.

schedule.text: Year-round classes and summer camps (dates not listed on the site); Shadow Company accepts high school students at any point; a Fringe show, When Tides Collide, is on sale (date not listed)

cost.text: No class, camp or ticket prices are listed; contact the group for pricing. The site mentions scholarships funded by donors.

first_step.how: Register a child for a year-round class or summer camp through the site, or have a high school student enroll in Shadow Company, where enrollment is open now
first_step.basis: Year-round programs are open for registration and the youth group takes new high school members at any point; the site does not say beginners are specifically welcomed.

records.notes: Most items have no month or year. The only dated item is a 2026 auction and holiday party fundraiser (month not stated), so no YYYY-MM sign of life is recorded. The Fringe show's year is not stated, and the page's copyright line (2025) is not used as evidence. Status is active on the strength of the 2026 event, so recheck before the site goes live. Volunteer, sponsorship and career details are under Support Us and the footer and were not read. The batch name is written 'Yes! And... Collaborative Arts' and the site's domain is yesandcamp.org.

notes: 18 of 18 batch groups written. Verdicts: publish 15, not_a_group 3 (Enchantment Theatre Company, Lyric Fest, Arcana New Music Ensemble). Statuses: active 14 (two of these, Lyric Fest and Arcana, are not_a_group), probably_active 2 (Enchantment Theatre Company, Network for New Music), dormant 1 (Lest We Forget Slavery Museum), unknown 1 (International Ballet Exchange). Judgment calls to review: Network for New Music (published on the strength of its paid double bass ensemble call; could be not_a_group), Lest We Forget Slavery Museum (dormant, newest dated item 2016), and Wildflower Composers (festival page dates conflict with its admissions note). Searches used: 0. Fetches: 29 attempts. Six first-pass calls failed on a shared domain safety rate limit; each of those six was fetched on a later single attempt. One guessed Wyck URL returned 404. The International Ballet Exchange domain now redirects to a parked for-sale page, which was not followed. Partner groups seen on other sites (Cliveden, Stenton, Awbury Arboretum, Johnson House, Germantown Historical Society, Hood Cemetery, La Salle University Art Museum, Symphony in C, the All City Orchestra) were not added to leads_only or fetched, because they fall outside this batch. leads_only is empty, so the rule to fetch leads does not apply to this run.
